title: New Aged Care Act
summary: From 1 November 2025 the Aged Care Act 2024 replaced the earlier aged care laws with a rights-based Act. Providers register in categories under one framework, and the Productivity Commission notes that provider registration is now more closely aligned with the NDIS.
direction_rationale: The Productivity Commission (2025) says the new Act came into force on 1 November 2025 and involved aligning some regulation with the NDIS, such as provider registration.

verified.notes: Assent from the Federal Register; the first compilation in force starts on 1 November 2025, matching the Productivity Commission's statement.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 29 October 2026 (tranche 3: laws in regulatory regimes with no register items) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Registration that is closer to the NDIS's should cut duplication for providers working in both sectors. The Act also adds duties and strengthened standards whose compliance cost has not been estimated, so the net effect is uncertain.

marks.reason: Provider registration is more closely aligned with NDIS requirements, reducing duplication for providers in both sectors.

assessment.confidence_note: The mark rests on the registration alignment the Productivity Commission describes; the costs of the Act's new duties were not found in the sources used.
